text:
jamie: noticing a cluster-wide uptick in local-SSD errors after last night's kernel-5.15.0-rc deploy. not full failures but big IOPS variance on GPU hosts.

devon: saw that on our ray pods — tails of high latencies, increased retry loops. telemetry shows bursty write stalls around 02:30 UTC.

sara: throwing some logs here. dmesg from host gpu-17:

```
[  754.233451] nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 error status: 0x4
[  754.233459] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
[  754.233488] nvme_core: Completing request with error
```

lee: smartctl output for the same device shows rising media and program fail counts (raw):

```
SMART overall-health self-assessment test result: FAILED
Media and Data Integrity Errors: 45
Program Fail Count: 12
Power-On Hours: 2160
```

jamie: important note — these hosts run heavy ephemeral-cleaner churn during evictions. cleaner concurrency was bumped last week to speed teardown for scaling tests.

devon: hypothesis: cleaner bursts + fstrim + kernel IO scheduler change combined to expose weak flash blocks -> transient remap causing long latency tails.

sara: reproduction notes — I ran fio on a repro host with same workload pattern and hit similar 200-400ms tail latencies on 4k random writes. iostat snippet:

```
Device            r/s     w/s     rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await  r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         12.00  1200.00  48.00  19200.00   16.00     0.90    10.20   0.10   10.30    1.00  98.5
```

lee: ops-bot flagged a subset of nodes in us-east-1 with high media errors and automatically cordoned 3 hosts. we should extend that to the whole pool until we triage.

ops-bot: Auto-action: cordoned nodes [gpu-17,gpu-53,gpu-68] due to host.metric.nvme_media_errors > 10 within 1h. :white_check_mark:

jamie: immediate runbook suggestion:
- scale down ephemeral-cleaner concurrency to 2 on affected pools
- add node selector to avoid scheduling new GPU pods on cordoned hosts
- enable delayed trimming: disable background fstrim during heavy churn windows
- start RMA for devices with program/media errors > 20

devon: +1. also propose reverting the kernel io_uring patch included in last deploy to confirm interaction. can we roll back just for a canary AZ?

sara: I'll create a canary rollout plan: patch kernel on two nodes in us-east-1a, then reproduce workload for 1 hour. if tail latency improves, we roll back across the rest.

lee: for medium-term: add a health check that bumps node weight down in scheduler when nvme media errors appear and stop live-scheduling heavy write workloads to hosts with any SMART errors.

jamie: last bit — action items assigned:
- sara -> canary test + report (ETA 2h)
- devon -> prepare kernel revert playbook and watch scripts (ETA 1h)
- lee -> update cleaner config and cordon policy (ETA 30m)
- infra -> open RMA with vendor for serials in the report (I'll do it)

sara: started the canary. attaching perf graphs in thread (uploaded). will post results.

devon: thanks team. ping me if cleaner throttling causes backlog, we can temporarily increase pod grace-periods to avoid mass evictions.

lee: noted, also enabling an alert for rising program_fail_count to catch earlier next time. :eyes:

jamie: great. keeping this thread live — we'll summarize the postmortem after the canary and device replacements. :thumbsup:
